selected_primary_idea.title: Resolution-Ladder Model Comparison for Pointlike Fermion Tests
selected_primary_idea.abstract: A versioned multi-channel likelihood framework that distinguishes pointlike Standard-Model, contact-interaction, finite-form-factor, and excited-fermion explanations while enforcing EFT validity and shared systematic uncertainty controls.
selected_primary_idea.scientific_object: quark and lepton pointlike behavior inferred through scattering observables, not direct visual imaging of constituents
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: A genuine short-distance deviation must have a channel-consistent dependence on momentum transfer and angular structure that remains distinguishable from nuisance and EFT-truncation effects.
selected_primary_idea.intervention: Vary momentum-transfer cut, operator set, form-factor scale, excited-state benchmark, nuisance priors, channel membership, and dimension-six/dimension-eight truncation policy.
selected_primary_idea.validation_protocol: Use synthetic closure tests, public-data-compatible interfaces when independently approved, held-out bins, and adversarial nuisance injections before any claim of a preferred hypothesis.
falsifiers: cross-channel coefficient inconsistency without a declared model
claim_boundaries: No identification of EFT coefficients with unique constituents.
No observed collisions or new limits are claimed by this proposal.

rejected_ideas.title: Prove that quarks and leptons are indivisible
rejected_ideas.reason: Exceeds the range-dependent, model-conditioned meaning of experimental pointlikeness.

rejected_ideas.title: Treat every EFT contact term as evidence for preons
rejected_ideas.reason: Violates the Survey invariant separating effective deviations from unique microscopic realization.

mcts_evolution_summary.result: Converted an ontological question into a finite-resolution model-comparison problem.
Separated contact, form-factor, and excited-state signatures from common nuisance mechanisms.
Selected a cutoff- and nuisance-stress-tested cross-channel likelihood as primary direction.
